Figure 6.28 Image Description 
This infographic shows the link between antibiotic use on farms and antibiotic resistant 
infections. It explains: when antibiotics are given to animals, the antibiotics kill most bacteria 
but resistant bacteria can survive and multiply. Those resistant bacteria can then spread in 
animal products, to produce through contaminated water or soil, to prepared food through 
contaminated surfaces (such as a cutting board previously used for contaminated food), and 
into the environment when animals poop. People become exposed to these bacteria and are 
sickened by them by consuming contaminated food or from the contaminated environment 
(especially farm workers). Resistant infections can cause mild illness or severe illness and may 
lead to death. About 1 in 5 resistant infections are caused by germs from food and animals.

infections? The CDC offers these tips, most of which are useful for reducing your risk of foodborne 
illness in general: 
• Take antibiotics only when needed.
